source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which behavior in a disaster survivor suggests post-traumatic stress disorder?
questions.rationale: PTSD is a sustained maladaptive response to trauma: flashbacks, recurrent dreams, irritability, sleep problems, detachment from others, and repressed memories.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q664 (PDF p. 883)
questions.quote: the client experiences recurrent and intrusive recollections of the event (flashbacks), has recurrent dreams of the event

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A dying client asks, 'Will you be the executor of my will?' What is the BEST reply?
questions.rationale: The question does not show why the client is asking. Seeking clarification acknowledges the request and keeps communication open.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q832 (PDF p. 1068)
questions.quote: In option 4, the nurse seeks clarification while acknowledging the client

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A charge nurse hears a nursing attendant shouting at a client with delirium. What is the PRIORITY action?
options: Tell the client all is well
Correct the attendant in the room
questions.rationale: The nurse first makes sure the client is safe, then talks to the attendant away from the client, who could become more confused or agitated.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q891 (PDF p. 1133)
questions.quote: The nurse must ascertain that the client is safe and then discuss the matter with the UAP in an area away from the hearing of the client.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which student statement on correcting a written chart error is CORRECT?
questions.rationale: Per agency policy, the nurse draws one line through the error, initials and dates it, then writes the correct information. Late entries are for omitted information.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1037 (PDF p. 1311)
questions.quote: Agency policy usually includes drawing one line through the error, initialing and dating the line, and then providing the correct information.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The nurse finds a client on the floor beside the bed. How should the incident report describe it?
questions.rationale: An incident report gives a factual description of what the nurse observed. The nurse did not see a fall, so only the finding is recorded.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1038 (PDF p. 1312)
questions.quote: The correct option is the only option that describes the facts as observed by the nurse.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The nurse finds a child's genitals swollen and suspects sexual abuse. What is of PRIMARY importance?
questions.rationale: The nurse's primary legal duty when abuse is suspected is to report it. In the Philippines, RA 7610 requires health workers to report suspected child abuse. Documenting and referring follow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1192 (PDF p. 1484)
questions.quote: The primary legal responsibility of the nurse when child abuse is suspected is to report the case.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A chemotherapy dose seems too high, and the prescriber is away for days. What should the nurse do NEXT?
questions.rationale: If an order seems wrong, the nurse clarifies it with the prescriber or a substitute before giving it. A pharmacist cannot change the dose.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1401 (PDF p. 1705)
questions.quote: the nurse must clarify the dosage with the client’s primary health care provider or the primary health care provider’s substitute before administering the medication.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Coworkers resist a nurse's plan for a restraint-free unit. What helps her MOST as a change agent?
options: Ask the supervisor to enforce it
questions.rationale: Change is more likely when the nurse works with others to solve shared problems than when she demands change alone.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1402 (PDF p. 1707)
questions.quote: To be an effective change agent, the nurse must work collaboratively with others to solve common problems.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A withdrawn client with end-stage heart failure won't join care. Which staff statement shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: A 'why' question asks for an explanation the client may not have, so it is nontherapeutic. The others acknowledge, explore feelings, or invite elaboration.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1418 (PDF p. 1724)
questions.quote: Requesting an explanation is a nontherapeutic communication technique.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which rehab client's needs can a nursing attendant MOST safely meet?
questions.rationale: Nursing attendants are trained to care for clients on bed rest and to maintain 24-hour urine collections, with instructions from the nurse.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1449 (PDF p. 1758)
questions.quote: Unlicensed assistive personnel are trained to care for the client on bed rest and to maintain 24-hour urine collections.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which client should the nurse care for FIRST?
questions.rationale: Numb fingers under a new cast may mean compartment syndrome, an emergency. Nerve and muscle damage start within 4 to 6 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1539 (PDF p. 1850)
questions.quote: The client with a cast who experiences numbness in the fingers should be seen first because this could be a symptom of compartment syndrome.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which client can be delegated to a nursing attendant?
questions.rationale: Attendants are trained to collect specimens such as clean-catch urine. Teaching, dressing care, and assessment need a nurse.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1549 (PDF p. 1862)
questions.quote: The UAP can assist with specimen collection such as a clean catch urine because he or she is trained in this skill.
